Merger Agreement Overview On October 28, 2026, Maplebear Inc., a Delaware corporation (the “ Company ”), entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with DoorDash, Inc., a Nevada corporation (“ Parent ”), and Ibiza Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent (“ Merger Sub ”). Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, and upon the terms and subject to the conditions described therein, Merger Sub will merge with and into the Company (the “ Merger ”), with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation in the Merger and a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent. The Board of Directors of the Company has unanimously approved the Merger Agreement and has recommended that the stockholders of the Company adopt the Merger Agreement. Closing Conditions The consummation of the Merger is subject to customary closing conditions, including, among other things, (i) adoption of the Merger Agreement by the Company’s stockholders, (ii) the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, as well as the expiration of any applicable mandatory waiting period, or the receipt of the applicable clearance or affirmative approval, under the Competition Act (Canada) and under the Israeli Economic Competition Law-1988, (iii) the absence of any order issued or law enacted by any governmental entity of competent jurisdiction preventing or prohibiting the consummation of the Merger, (iv) the effectiveness of a registration statement on Form S-4 to be filed by Parent registering the shares of Parent Class A Common Stock (or Parent Class C Common Stock, if applicable) issuable in the Merger, (v) authorization for listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market of the shares of Parent Class A Common Stock (or Parent Class C Common Stock, if applicable) issuable in the Merger and (vi) certain other conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement. Merger Consideration; Election and Proration Procedures At the effective time of the Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), each issued and outstanding share of common stock, par value $0.0001 per share, of the Company (the “ Shares ”), other than Shares owned by (i) the Company, Parent, Merger Sub or any direct or indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Parent or the Company and (ii) stockholders of the Company who have validly exercised their statutory rights of appraisal under Section 262 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, will be converted into the right to receive: (i) if a cash election (a “ Cash Election ”) has been properly made and not revoked or deemed revoked in accordance with the requirements set forth in the Merger Agreement, $65.00 in cash, without interest (the “ Cash Consideration ”); (ii) if an election to receive Parent Class A Common Stock (a “ Stock Election ”) has been properly made and not revoked or deemed revoked in accordance with the requirements set forth in the Merger Agreement, 0.3372 shares of Parent Class A Common Stock (the “ Stock Exchange Ratio ”), subject to Parent’s election to issue the Alternative Stock Consideration (as defined below), without interest (the “ Stock Consideration ”); (iii) if both a Cash Election and a Stock Election (a “ Mixed Election ”) have been properly made and not revoked or deemed revoked in accordance with the requirements set forth in the Merger Agreement, a combination of $48.75 in cash, without interest, plus 0.08430 shares of Parent Class A Common Stock (the “ Mixed Exchange Ratio ”), subject to Parent’s election to issue the Alternative Stock Consideration, without interest (the “ Mixed Consideration ” and, together with the Cash Consideration and the Stock Consideration, the “ Merger Consideration ”); or (iv) if neither a Cash Election nor a Stock Election has been properly made (a “ Non-Election Share ”), the Cash Consideration. Parent may elect to issue shares of Parent Class C Common Stock in lieu of Parent Class A Common Stock (the “ Alternative Stock Consideration ”) as the Stock Consideration and the stock portion of the Mixed Consideration, subject to, and in accordance with, the terms set forth in the Merger Agreement. Any such election (i) must be made prior to the earlier of (x) March 31, 2027 and (y) three months prior to the closing of the Merger, (ii) is subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions, including listing the Parent Class C Common Stock on Nasdaq and the issuance by Parent of a dividend of at least 0.5 shares of Parent Class C Common Stock on each outstanding share of Parent Class A Common Stock and Parent Class B Common Stock and (iii) requires Parent to provide the Company with prior, irrevocable written notice. If Parent elects to issue the Alternative Stock Consideration, the Stock Exchange Ratio and the Mixed Exchange Ratio will be adjusted to provide for an upward adjustment of the Stock Exchange Ratio and Mixed Exchange Ratio applicable to the Parent Class C Common Stock if the Parent Closing Price (as defined below) of the Parent Class C Common Stock is less than the Parent Closing Price of the Parent Class A Common Stock so that the Company’s stockholders receive the same value as they would have received in Parent Class A Common Stock, subject to, and in accordance with, the terms set forth in the Merger Agreement. 2 Each record holder of Shares will have the right to submit an election specifying the portion of such holder’s Shares with respect to which such holder desires to make a Cash Election, a Stock Election or a Mixed Election, using a form of election to be prepared by Parent and reasonably acceptable to the Company (the “ Form of Election ”). The Company and Parent will mail the Form of Election not less than 20 business days prior to the anticipated deadline for making an election to holders of record as of the fifth business day prior to such mailing date, which deadline will be 5:00 p.m. local time (in the city in which the principal office of the Exchange Agent is located) on the date that is three business days prior to the parties’ good faith estimate of the closing date of the Merger, or such other date as the Company and Parent may mutually agree (the “ Election Deadline ”). If the closing date is delayed to a subsequent date, the Election Deadline will be similarly delayed to a subsequent date. An election will be properly made only if the exchange agent for the Merger (the “ Exchange Agent ”) receives a properly completed and executed Form of Election prior to the Election Deadline. Holders may change their election by written notice accompanied by a properly completed and executed revised Form of Election or revoke an election by written notice to the Exchange Agent at any time prior to the Election Deadline, and any Shares as to which no valid election is in effect at the Election Deadline will be treated as Non-Election Shares. All elections will be automatically deemed revoked if the Merger Agreement is terminated. The Exchange Agent will have reasonable discretion to determine whether an election, revocation or change has been properly or timely made. The Merger Agreement includes a proration mechanism pursuant to which the total number of Shares to be converted into the right to receive the Stock Consideration will not exceed a maximum number of Shares, calculated so that the aggregate stock portion of the Merger Consideration issued in respect of Shares subject to Stock Elections and Mixed Elections does not exceed the amount that would have been issued had all Shares that converted into the right to receive the Merger Consideration received the Mixed Consideration, as determined in accordance with the terms set forth in the Merger Agreement. If the aggregate number of Shares with respect to which Stock Elections are properly made and not revoked or deemed revoked exceeds such maximum number, then each electing holder’s Shares subject to a Stock Election will be converted automatically into the right to receive the Stock Consideration only with respect to a pro rata portion of such Shares (based on the ratio of such maximum number to the aggregate number of Shares subject to Stock Elections), with the holder’s remaining Shares that are subject to a Stock Election instead converting into the right to receive the Cash Consideration. Treatment of Company Equity Awards Each option to purchase Shares outstanding and unexercised immediately prior to the Effective Time will be canceled, and, to the extent vested (after giving effect to any vesting that occurs automatically as a result of the Merger) and having a per-share exercise price less than the Cash Consideration, converted into the right to receive a cash payment equal to the excess of the Cash Consideration over the per-share exercise price, multiplied by the number of Shares subject to such option. Each award of Company restricted stock units and Company performance stock units that is outstanding, vested and unsettled as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (after giving effect to any vesting that occurs automatically as a result of the Merger) will be canceled and converted into the right to receive, in respect of each Share subject to such award, the Cash Consideration. Each award of Company restricted stock units and Company performance stock units that is outstanding and unvested as of immediately prior to the Effective Time (after giving effect to any vesting that occurs automatically as a result of the Merger) will be canceled immediately prior to the Effective Time, and, as soon as practicable following, but in no more than five days following, the Effective Time, Parent will grant to each holder of such an award a Parent restricted stock unit award (each, a “ Parent Restricted Stock Unit Award ”) with respect to a number of shares of Parent Class A Common Stock (or, if Parent elects to issue the Alternative Stock Consideration, Parent Class C Common Stock) (rounded to the nearest whole share) equal to the product of (A) the number of Shares subject to such award of Company restricted stock units or award of Company performance stock units immediately prior to the Effective Time (with the number of Shares subject to awards of Company performance stock units determined by deeming the applicable performance goals achieved at the greater of target performance and actual performance through the Effective Time (as determined by the Company’s Board of Directors in good faith)) and (B) the Equity Award Exchange Ratio. Each Parent Restricted Stock Unit Award shall vest in substantially equal installments on each of Parent’s standard quarterly vesting dates (but no later than a vesting date permitted by the terms of the related Company restricted stock unit award as in effect prior to the Effective Time) that occur between the Effective Time and the end of the vesting schedule that applied to the related award of Company performance stock units (or end of the performance period if no vesting schedule applied to the Company performance stock units) or Company restricted stock units, and shall otherwise be subject to the same terms and conditions as were applicable to the related award of Company performance stock units or Company restricted stock units under the applicable Company equity incentive plan and award agreement as of immediately prior to the Effective Time. The “ Equity Award Exchange Ratio ” is a fraction, the numerator of which is the sum of $48.75 in cash and an amount equal to the product of the Mixed Exchange Ratio and the Parent Closing Price and the denominator of which is the Parent Closing Price. The “ Parent Closing Price ” is the volume-weighted average trading price of Parent Class A Common Stock (or Parent Class C Common Stock if Parent elects to issue the Alternative Stock Consideration) for the five consecutive trading days ending on (and including) the trading day immediately prior to the date of the Effective Time. 3 Representations, Warranties and Covenants The Merger Agreement includes representations and warranties and covenants of the parties customary for a transaction of this nature. Until the earlier of the termination of the Merger Agreement and the Effective Time, the Company has agreed to use reasonable best efforts to conduct its business in the ordinary course consistent with past practice in all material respects and has agreed to certain other operating covenants, and Parent has agreed to certain operating covenants, in each case as set forth more fully in the Merger Agreement. The Merger Agreement requires that Parent and the Company use reasonable best efforts to take all actions and do all things necessary, proper or advisable to complete the Merger as promptly as reasonably practicable, and in any event prior to the Outside Date (as defined below), including, among other things, (i) defending or contesting any proceedings (including through final, non-appealable judgment) challenging the Merger Agreement or the consummation of the transactions contemplated thereby and (ii) in the case of Parent, proposing, negotiating, committing to and effecting certain remedy actions as may be required in connection with seeking regulatory approvals, except as would have a Regulatory Material Adverse Effect (as defined in the Merger Agreement), in each case on the terms and subject to the conditions specified in the Merger Agreement. In addition, Parent has agreed to commit to certain specified commitments to grocers, merchants and consumers, which commitments will not be taken into account in determining whether a Regulatory Material Adverse Effect would occur. (October 27, 2026 / GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Central Bancompany, Inc. (Nasdaq: CBC) (“Central Bancompany”, “the Company”, or “CBC”), the bank holding company for The Central Trust Bank (the “Bank”), today announced preliminary financial results for the third quarter 2026. John “JR” Ross, President and Chief Executive Officer of Central Bancompany, commented: “We delivered another strong quarter, supported by continued balance sheet growth, disciplined expense management, and solid credit quality. Adjusted net income1 increased $13.7 million from a year ago and $2.8 million from the prior quarter. Year-over-year performance reflected growth in net interest income and noninterest income that outpaced expense growth, while linked-quarter results benefited from continued net interest margin expansion and higher net interest income driven by our asset-sensitive balance sheet. These favorable trends were partially offset by lower mortgage banking revenues.” Ross continued, “Underlying business fundamentals remained healthy across our franchise. Average total deposits increased more than 4% from the prior-year quarter, including 6% growth in noninterest-bearing deposits, while average loans grew at an annualized rate of more than 3% from the prior quarter despite our continued focus on reducing certain consumer loan balances. Credit quality remained benign, and we maintained our allowance for credit losses coverage ratio while modestly increasing the overall reserve balance to support loan growth.” “We also continue to align our leadership talent with our strongest growth opportunities. Matthew Adams has been named President and CEO of our Oklahoma market, and Brandy Bryant, formerly a Mid-Missouri market CEO, has assumed a new enterprise leadership role focused on consumer and small business credit products and processes. Both are accomplished leaders with more than 20 years of experience with our company and are well positioned to support continued growth and execution across our franchise.” “These results reflect the resilience of our business model, the strength of our customer relationships, and the dedication of our associates across all of our markets.” Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin Net interest income totaled $218.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, increasing from both the prior year period and prior quarter, reflecting growth in average earning assets and expansion in net interest margin. Net interest margin increased to 4.48% (4.51% on an FTE basis1), compared with 4.36% in the prior year quarter and 4.40% in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven by higher loan and securities yields, continued loan growth, a favorable earning asset mix, and lower balances of interest-earning cash. Period-end loans exceeded the quarterly average by $54 million, providing positive momentum entering the fourth quarter. Average total deposits grew 4% year-over-year to $15.4 billion, driven by continued growth in both noninterest-bearing and interest- bearing non-maturity deposits. Provision for credit losses The provision for credit losses was $4.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 14.2% from the prior quarter driven primarily by loan growth. Noninterest expense Total noninterest expense was $131.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $4.0 million, or 3.2% compared to the third quarter of 2025. Expense growth remained well below our revenue growth rate, reflecting continued expense discipline and positive operating leverage. Salaries and employee benefits totaled $80.0 million, remaining stable compared with the prior quarter while increasing $4.7 million, or 6.3%, from the prior year quarter, primarily due to annual merit increases and higher performance-based compensation. This increase was partially offset by lower non-personnel expenses, including legal and professional fees, which declined $0.9 million, or 13.9%, reflecting lower technology consulting costs compared to the prior year quarter. Occupancy and technology expenses also declined modestly from the prior year period. The efficiency ratio (FTE)1 improved to 45.4% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 46.1% in the prior quarter and 47.7% in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting our ability to grow revenues at a faster rate than expenses. (Nasdaq: CBC) (“Central Bancompany”, “the Company”, or “CBC”), the bank holding company for The Central Trust Bank (the “Bank”), today announced preliminary financial results for the second quarter 2026. John “JR” Ross, President and Chief Executive Officer of Central Bancompany, commented "We are pleased to announce another set of solid financial results for Central in the second quarter of 2026. Second quarter net income was $113.8 million, or $0.47 per fully diluted share, reflecting a 2.24% ROA and a 25% fee income ratio, despite continued growth in net interest income. We are again encouraged by loan growth in the quarter, with ending loans excluding other consumer up approximately 6% annualized quarter-over- quarter. Average deposits grew by $0.4 billion, or 3%, including growth of over $276 million in average noninterest-bearing demand balances from the prior year quarter’s balances.” “Our second quarter financial results reflect the strength of our diversified and customer-centric business model,” Ross continued. “We are fortunate to report another quarter of steady growth heading into the second half of the year. We also continue to invest in our underpenetrated metro markets, opening three new full-service branches during the second quarter to support our long-term growth strategy. While economic conditions remain generally favorable, we are mindful that uncertainty persists across the macroeconomic and geopolitical landscape. I would like to thank our teammates for their tireless efforts delivering for our clients, communities and fellow shareholders.” Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin The Company reported net interest income of $212.8 million in the second quarter of 2026, reflecting a net interest margin of 4.40% (4.43% on an FTE basis1). Net interest income increased $17.7 million from the second quarter of 2025, driven by NIM expansion and solid underlying average earning asset growth of $1.1 billion, or 6%, resulting from deposit growth and higher capital. In the second quarter of 2026, loans grew at an annualized rate of 6%, excluding the reduction in other consumer loans, and net interest margin increased to 4.40% from 4.26% in the prior year quarter. Average earning assets for the quarter totaled $19.4 billion, a decrease of $0.2 billion, or 1%, from the prior quarter. The decrease in average earning assets from the prior quarter was largely driven by a seasonal decrease in average deposits. Average total loans held for investment were $11.6 billion for the second quarter of 2026, an increase of $0.1 billion, or 1% from the prior quarter, despite deemphasizing indirect consumer lending, which declined $37.8 million from the prior quarter’s average. Excluding other consumer loans, average total loans held for investment increased $177.6 million or 2% over the prior quarter due to loan growth spread across a number of categories and markets. Total loans ended the quarter at $11.7 billion, $92 million above the average for the quarter, reflecting continued loan growth momentum. (NYSE: HZO) (“MarineMax” or the “Company”), a boat and yacht retailer, marina operator, and superyacht services company, today announced results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and full year ended September 30, 2026. Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter Summary • Revenue of $520.1 million • Same-store sales decreased 5.7% • Gross margin increased 270 basis points to 37.4% • Net loss attributable to MarineMax of $13.0 million • Net loss per share of $0.59; adjusted net loss per share 1 of $0.08 • Adjusted EBITDA 1 of $21.8 million Fiscal 2026 Full Year Summary • Revenue of $2.2 billion • Same-store sales decreased 5.5% • Gross margin increased 240 basis points to 34.9% • Net loss attributable to MarineMax of $8.2 million • Net loss per share of $0.37; adjusted earnings per diluted share 1 of $0.58 • Adjusted EBITDA 1 of $112.6 million CEO and President Commentary “Fiscal 2026 demonstrated the strength of MarineMax's diversified business model and the benefits of our strategic investments to broaden our marine offerings and expand our presence in durable, higher-margin businesses,” said Brett McGill, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and President. “Despite a challenging retail environment, contributions from across our portfolio helped offset market pressures, underscoring the value of our diversification strategy. Since 2019, we have expanded our higher-margin, non-boat revenue streams, contributing to a significant improvement in gross margin from 26.1% in fiscal 2019 to 34.9% in fiscal 2026. I want to thank our team members, whose continued dedication and commitment to our customers have made these results possible. “Our previously announced agreement to be acquired by Safe Harbor represents an important milestone for MarineMax and reflects the value we have created by building a broader and more diversified marine business,” McGill continued. “The combination of our complementary businesses will create opportunities to improve our offerings, deepen customer and industry relationships, and support continued growth. As we move toward completing the transaction, we remain focused on serving our customers, supporting our partners, and executing our strategic priorities across the business.” Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter Results Revenue totaled $520.1 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $552.2 million in the prior-year period. The decrease primarily reflected lower boat sales, partially offset by continued growth in several higher-margin areas of the business, including marinas and parts and service. Gross profit increased to $194.3 million, or 37.4% of revenue, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $191.4 million, or 34.7% of revenue, in the prior-year period. The 270 basis point expansion in gross margin was primarily driven by improved boat profitability and a greater contribution from higher-margin businesses across the portfolio. Selling, general and administrative (SG&A) expenses totaled $196.1 million, or 37.7% of revenue, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $177.6 million, or 32.2% of revenue, in the prior-year period. The increase was primarily attributable to costs associated with the Company's pending acquisition by Safe Harbor Marinas (“Safe Harbor”). Excluding transaction and other costs, intangible amortization, changes in contingent consideration, weather-related costs and restructuring expenses, Adjusted SG&A 1 increased $3.2 million, or 1.8%, to $181.1 million, compared with $177.9 million in the prior-year period. Interest expense decreased to $13.2 million, or 2.5% of revenue, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $17.3 million, or 3.1% of revenue, in the prior-year period. Net loss attributable to MarineMax was $13.0 million, or $0.59 per share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with a net loss attributable to MarineMax of $0.9 million, or $0.04 per share, in the prior-year period. The Company reported an adjusted net loss of $1.8 million, or $0.08 per share, compared with an adjusted net loss of $1.1 million, or $0.05 per share, in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA increased 26% to $21.8 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $17.3 million in the prior-year period. Balance Sheet Cash and cash equivalents totaled $156.4 million as of September 30, 2026, compared with $170.4 million at the end of the prior-year period. Inventories declined $54.6 million, or 6.3%, to $812.8 million in fiscal 2026 from $867.3 million at the end of fiscal 2025, which followed a $39.3 million decline in inventory from the end of fiscal 2024. Acquisition by Safe Harbor As previously announced on August 10, 2026, MarineMax has entered into a definitive agreement with Safe Harbor, a marina and superyacht service business, under which Safe Harbor will acquire all issued and outstanding shares of common stock of MarineMax for $53.00 per share in cash, representing an enterprise value of approximately $1.5 billion. The transaction, which was unanimously approved by the Company’s Board of Directors, is expected to close by the end of the calendar year 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including the approval of MarineMax’s shareholders. In light of the Company's pending acquisition by Safe Harbor, MarineMax will not hold a conference call to discuss its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and full year financial results and does not intend to provide financial guidance for fiscal 2027. About MarineMax As a boat and yacht retailer, marina operator and superyacht services company, MarineMax (NYSE: HZO) is United by Water. We have over 120 locations worldwide, including over 70 dealerships and over 65 marina and storage facilities. Our integrated business includes IGY Marinas, which operates luxury marinas in yachting and sport fishing destinations around the world; Fraser Yachts Group and Northrop & Johnson, leading superyacht brokerage and luxury yacht services companies; Cruisers Yachts, one of the world’s premier manufacturers of premium sport yachts, motor yachts, and Aviara luxury dayboats; and Intrepid Powerboats, a premier manufacturer of powerboats. To enhance and simplify the customer experience, we provide financing and insurance services as well as leading digital technology products that connect boaters to a network of preferred marinas, dealers, and marine professionals through Boatyard and Boatzon. Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. Agreement and Plan of Merger On October 26, 2026, MidCap Financial Investment Corporation, a Maryland corporation (“ MFIC ”), entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “ Merger Agreement ”) with Ares Capital Corporation, a Maryland corporation (“ ARCC ”); Union Acquisition Sub Inc., a Maryland corporation and a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of ARCC (“ Acquisition Sub 1 ”); Union Acquisition Sub LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and a direct wholly-owned subsidiary of ARCC (“ Acquisition Sub 2 ”); and, solely for the limited purposes set forth therein, Ares Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company and the external investment adviser to ARCC (“ ACM ”). The Merger Agreement provides that, subject to the conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the First Merger (the “ Effective Time ”), Acquisition Sub 1 will be merged with and into MFIC (the “ First Merger ”), with MFIC continuing as the surviving company and as a wholly-owned subsidiary of ARCC. Immediately after the Effective Time, MFIC will merge with and into Acquisition Sub 2 (the “ Second Merger ” and, together with the First Merger, the “ Mergers ”), with Acquisition Sub 2 continuing as the surviving company and as a wholly-owned subsidiary of ARCC. The board of directors of MFIC (the “ MFIC Board ”), on the recommendation of a special committee comprised solely of disinterested directors of MFIC (the “ Special Committee ”), has unanimously approved, among other things, the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Mergers (the “ Transactions ”). The board of directors of ARCC has also unanimously approved the Merger Agreement and the Transactions. The parties to the Merger Agreement intend for the Mergers, taken together, to be treated as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “ Code ”). Holders of MFIC Common Stock (as defined below) will not be entitled to appraisal or objecting stockholder rights in connection with the Mergers. Merger Consideration Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, at the Effective Time, each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of MFIC (“ MFIC Common Stock ”) issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than shares held by a subsidiary of MFIC or held, directly or indirectly, by ARCC or Acquisition Sub 1) will be converted into the right to receive (i) $1.21 in cash, without interest, to be paid by ACM (the “ Cash Consideration ”), and (ii) a number of validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable shares of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of ARCC (“ ARCC Common Stock ”) equal to the Exchange Ratio (as defined below), with cash to be paid in lieu of fractional shares, if applicable (together with the Cash Consideration, the “ Merger Consideration ”). Based on the terms of the Merger Agreement, as of the date of the Merger Agreement, the Merger Consideration represents total consideration of $10.88 per fully diluted share of MFIC Common Stock, consisting of approximately $1.21 per share in cash and approximately $9.67 per share in ARCC Common Stock, subject to adjustment as described below. The “ Exchange Ratio ” will be determined as of a date mutually agreed by the parties that is no earlier than 48 hours (excluding Sundays and holidays) prior to the Effective Time, based on ARCC’s net asset value per share (“ ARCC NAV ”) and the closing price of ARCC Common Stock on that date (the “ ARCC Price ”), as follows: (1) if the ARCC Price is less than or equal to 100% of ARCC NAV, the Exchange Ratio will equal $9.67 less the Post-Signing Tax Dividend Amount (as defined below), divided by ARCC NAV; (2) if the ARCC Price is greater than 100% but less than or equal to 104.5% of ARCC NAV, the Exchange Ratio will equal the product of (A) $9.67 less the Post-Signing Tax Dividend Amount and (B) 1.00 plus 50% of the premium of the ARCC Price to ARCC NAV, divided by the ARCC Price; and (3) if the ARCC Price is greater than 104.5% of ARCC NAV, the Exchange Ratio will equal the product of (A) $9.67 less the Post-Signing Tax Dividend Amount and (B) 102.25%, divided by the ARCC Price. Tax Distribution Prior to the closing of the Mergers, MFIC will declare one or more dividends in order to distribute all of its previously undistributed investment company taxable income, any prior year shortfall and net capital gain and to maintain its qualification as a “regulated investment company” under the Code (any such dividend, a “ Tax Dividend ”). The stock portion of the Merger Consideration will be reduced by the aggregate per share amount of any Tax Dividend declared after the date of the Merger Agreement with a record date on or prior to the closing date, excluding regular quarterly dividends (the “ Post-Signing Tax Dividend Amount ”). Termination Rights The Merger Agreement contains customary termination rights for each of MFIC and ARCC, including if the First Merger has not been consummated within nine months after the date of the Merger Agreement (subject to an automatic three-month extension in certain circumstances), or if MFIC’s stockholders do not approve the Mergers. MFIC may terminate the Merger Agreement, prior to obtaining stockholder approval, to enter into a definitive agreement providing for a superior proposal, on the terms and conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement. ARCC may terminate the Merger Agreement if, among other things, the MFIC Board changes its recommendation. MFIC will be required to pay ARCC a termination fee of $31,360,000 upon termination of the Merger Agreement under certain specified circumstances. Representations, Warranties and Covenants The Merger Agreement contains customary representations and warranties by each of MFIC, ARCC, Acquisition Sub 1, Acquisition Sub 2 and ACM, subject to specific exceptions and qualifications. The Merger Agreement also contains customary covenants, including, among others, covenants relating to the operation of each of MFIC’s and ARCC’s businesses during the period prior to closing of the Mergers, the preparation of a registration statement on Form N-14 (the “ Registration Statement ”) and the holding of a special meeting of the stockholders of MFIC. MFIC has agreed to convene and hold a stockholder meeting for the purpose of obtaining the approval of the Mergers by MFIC’s stockholders and has agreed to recommend that its stockholders approve the Mergers. MFIC has also agreed to suspend its share repurchase program. The Merger Agreement includes restrictions on the ability of MFIC or its subsidiaries to solicit proposals for alternative transactions or initiate or otherwise engage in discussions regarding such proposals, subject to exceptions and termination provisions. However, the MFIC Board, acting upon the recommendation of the Special Committee, may, subject to certain conditions, change its recommendation to MFIC’s stockholders, terminate the Merger Agreement and enter into an agreement with respect to a superior proposal, or change its recommendation in response to an intervening event if it determines in good faith, after consultation with its financial advisor and outside legal counsel, that the failure to do so would reasonably be expected to be inconsistent with the directors’ duties under applicable law. Conditions to the Mergers Consummation of the Mergers, which is currently anticipated to occur during the first half of calendar year 2027, is subject to certain closing conditions, including, but not limited to, (1) requisite approval of MFIC’s stockholders, (2) the authorization for listing on the NASDAQ Global Select Market of the ARCC Common Stock to be issued as consideration in the First Merger, (3) effectiveness of the Registration Statement for the ARCC Common Stock to be issued as consideration in the First Merger, (4) the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended, (5) the absence of certain legal impediments to the consummation of the Mergers and (6) subject to certain exceptions, the accuracy of the representations and warranties and compliance with the covenants of each party to the Merger Agreement. The obligation of ARCC to consummate the Mergers is further conditioned upon the receipt of certain third party consents.
